name: Self-Driving Agent from Scratch
description: A from-scratch implementation of Deep Q-Network (DQN) that learns to drive in the CarRacing-v3 environment using only pixel input.
longDesc: This project implements a Deep Q-Network agent from scratch using PyTorch to master the CarRacing-v3 environment from Gymnasium. The agent learns entirely from raw pixel input — receiving 96x96 RGB frames and deciding when to steer, accelerate, or brake. The implementation includes a CNN architecture that processes 4 stacked grayscale frames to detect motion, an experience replay buffer to break temporal correlation in training data, a target network for stable Q-value estimation, and epsilon-greedy exploration that decays over time. Key challenges included frame preprocessing (cropping, grayscale conversion, normalization), tuning hyperparameters like learning rate and epsilon decay, and implementing checkpoint saving to resume training across sessions. The project demonstrates understanding of core RL concepts including the Bellman equation, Q-learning, and the exploration-exploitation tradeoff.

name: Calibration Workflow Redesign
description: Redesigned the sensor calibration workflow for EMG research software.
longDesc: I redesigned an EMG calibration workflow at a global software company* specializing in wearable sensors, a critical step that allows researchers to normalize sensors to participants' muscles for accurate study results. I overhauled the UX, UI, and user flows, introducing multi-sensor calibration to save researchers time while increasing consistency and reliability in their data collection. This project was completed in collaboration with a team of three, highlighting both coordination and design problem-solving in a fast-paced environment. *Project details and designs withheld for privacy.

name: Balancing Act
description: A reinforcement learning agent trained to balance a pole on a moving cart, achieving perfect scores using Proximal Policy Optimization.
longDesc: This project explores the fundamentals of reinforcement learning by training an agent to solve the classic CartPole control problem. Using Stable Baselines3 and OpenAI Gymnasium, I implemented a PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) agent that learns to balance a pole on a cart by applying left or right forces. The agent observes cart position, cart velocity, pole angle, and pole angular velocity, then decides which direction to push. Before training, the agent averaged around 20 reward per episode with inconsistent, poor performance. After 20,000 timesteps of training, the agent achieved perfect 500/500 scores across all evaluation episodes — effectively solving the environment. This project served as my introduction to RL concepts including policy gradients, reward signals, and the exploration-exploitation tradeoff.

name: Split
description: A mobile-first bill splitting app that lets groups upload receipts, assign items, and instantly calculate who owes whom.
longDesc: Split is a product-focused web app designed to remove the friction from splitting group expenses. Users can upload a receipt photo or manually enter items, review and edit line items, add people to a group, and assign each item to one or more people. The app calculates per-person subtotals, proportionally distributes tax and tip, and generates a clear settlement summary showing who owes whom and how much. The project emphasizes clean UX flows, state management for complex shared data, and thoughtful edge-case handling (unassigned items, shared items, mobile responsiveness). It showcases end-to-end product thinking from user stories and MVP scoping through to front-end implementation and derived state calculations.

name: Echo
description: Analyzes user reviews for places with sentiment analysis.
longDesc: A React web app that displays insights on user reviews of a searched query. These insights include graphs with breakdowns of positive, negative, neutral reviews, sentiment over time, and an AI-generated summary of most recent reviews. The app helps users quickly understand public opinion about different places without sifting through hundreds of reviews. All information fetched from an external API.

caseStudy.problem: Users had to sift through hundreds of online reviews to get a sense of public opinion.
caseStudy.goal: Create a tool to surface review trends and sentiment in a digestible visual format.
caseStudy.approach: I designed several UI iterations in Figma focusing on clarity and visual hierarchy. Key metrics like overview, sentiment breakdown and images were prioritized.

designIterations.title: Low-Fidelity Mock
designIterations.notes: Created a basic layout framework with placeholder elements to establish general page structure. Visual styling was minimal, with no defined hierarchy or content yet. Feedback focused on maintaining clean separation between blocks to avoid clutter.

designIterations.title: Mid-Fidelity Mock
designIterations.notes: Introduced content and visual hierarchy through grouped sections, light gray backgrounds, and clear labels. This version helped validate layout logic and user flows.

designIterations.title: Final Design
designIterations.notes: Final iteration applied a polished visual style and color scheme, enhancing clarity and engagement. The organization of each section was very strategic, prioritizing high level information first and more specific details later. Each section was differentiated with dark backgrounds, accent colors, and refined typography. Interactive elements and data visualizations were styled for readability. This version addressed clutter concerns and clearly guided the user's eye across the content.

outcomes: Improved user understanding of sentiment breakdown at a glance
Positive feedback on design clarity and speed of insights
First project to integrate D3.js charts

name: strategy.town
description: A project in which I extended current functionality with new user stories.
longDesc: The project extended existing single-player functionality to support real-time multiplayer interactions, user progress tracking, and personalized statistics dashboards. Players can track wins, streaks, and scores over time, adding a competitive and engaging layer to the games. The project demonstrates both front-end development skills and system design thinking required to manage multiplayer game state and user data.
